title: Recover a caught sample carrier with coordinated two-arm motion
instruction: Move the sample carrier onto the receiving stand, keeping the samples upright and contained. If it catches, stop and free it without forcing or tipping it, then complete the transfer.
context: The carrier is stored under a retaining lip on one side. Continuing the other arm’s lift while that side is caught can tip the shared load and topple its samples. The robot must preserve balance and clear the obstruction; clearing it before lifting is equally valid.
setup: A 120 by 240 mm carrier holds four independent rigid capped dummy tubes, each 30 mm in diameter with a 72 mm body. Two 64 mm grip bars are 280 mm apart, each on a passive revolute connection. An orange retaining lip overlaps one ear at the source stand. A second stand is 165 mm away along the transfer direction. Original primitive assets and the YAM station.
scoring: Historical zero if carrier tilt exceeds 12 degrees or any sampled bottom-circumference point exits the carrier bounds. 0.5 when the complete carrier is clear of the source stand, level within 5 degrees, with all samples contained and upright within 10 degrees. 1.0 when the carrier is within 10 mm and 5 degrees of its receiving pose, samples upright within 10 degrees, both grippers released and clear, and stable for 1 second.
fidelity: Rigid carrier, capped rigid dummy samples and fixed retaining lip. Passive revolute grip bars approximate folding supports. No liquids, material deformation or actuator faults. Thresholds are design values; no claim that every real carrier requires two hands.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 (2400 steps); scripted physical demo: 1.0 (600 steps).
reset_notes: Restore the carrier to its source stand with its left ear under the lip, place all four capped dummy tubes upright at their starting marks, and reset both arms. Reset clears the historical failure latch. Trials use the fixed layout with object_jitter=0 and seed 42.
